title: Temporary capacity fallbacks and metering policy for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a transparent, operator-friendly policy for short-lived capacity boosts on Dedicated fleets. This ticket scopes: (1) a runtime allocator that grants ephemeral capacity when Dedicated nodes experience transient load spikes, (2) a metering model that attributes excess usage to burst envelopes with clear invoice signals, and (3) controls and safeguards to preserve throughput guarantees for committed capacity. Goal: reduce customer outages from short bursts while avoiding opaque overage surprises.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator grants ephemeral capacity (up to X% of fleet) with a configurable decay window and per-tenant priority vectors
Burst usage is recorded in a separate "metering envelope" that appears in billing exports with start/end timestamps and breakdown by route/model
Operator can manually revoke or quarantine ephemeral capacity and see real-time candidates in Console (list + metrics)
Throughput SLO for committed capacity remains unchanged in synthetic tests under burst conditions
E2E test coverage for allocator behavior, billing attribution, and rollback paths in CI
work_summary: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after on-call incident where two Dedicated tenants consumed transient GPU cycles and triggered unpredictable throttling and invoices. Linked incident runbook.

2026-02-25: Design sync with Product & Billing. Decided to separate burst metering into a distinct envelope rather than mixing with committed usage. Billing agreed to a human-readable invoice section for burst events.

2026-03-02: Prototype allocator implemented in staging: 'ephemeral-reservoir' module that uses token-buckets per-region and per-fleet. Initial implementation supports max 15% overcommit per-fleet and a 10-minute half-life decay.

2026-03-06: Load test (synthetic) showed sustained 60s spikes are handled without violating latency SLO for committed capacity; observed tail latency regressions for low-priority tenants — added preemption thresholds.

2026-03-10: Billing export schema updated. New fields: burst_envelope_id, burst_start_iso, burst_end_iso, burst_tokens_consumed, attribution_policy. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/214
2026-03-12: Security and Legal reviewed invoice language for clarity. Minor phrasing changes agreed. Preparing a Console UI mock for operator controls and tenant notifications.
technical_design: Allocator: ephemeral-reservoir runs as a control-plane actor that accepts capacity requests; decision inputs: tenant priority score, current committed utilization, recent burst history, region headroom, and operator-configured hard caps
Priority vector: combines customer tier, SLA flags, and recent fairness weight (exponential decay) to avoid repeated exploitation of burst buckets
Decay policy: per-burst energy modeled as an exponential decay (half-life configurable per-customer), plus a global reservoir refill schedule to avoid permanent depletion

Preemption: ephemeral capacity is preemptible by committed capacity. Preemption order: 1) current ephemeral requests, 2) non-critical low-tier ephemeral allocations, 3) oldest ephemeral allocations — designed to preserve tail SLOs for committed tenants

Metering: all ephemeral allocations emit a burst_envelope record to our usage pipeline (Kafka topic 'burst-metering'). Records include bucket_id, tenant, model, tokens, peak_rps, start_ts, end_ts, and preemption_events

Billing model: billing service consumes burst_envelope and produces a separate invoice line item. Billing rules are configurable: flat-per-minute rate, usage-based per-token, or hybrid. Pilot will use hybrid: base per-minute + per-token tail surcharge
Operator controls: Console will expose: global burst enable/disable, per-fleet hard cap (absolute GPU count), per-tenant quarantine toggle, and live candidate list with cancel/commit actions

Safeguards: guardrails include: max_burst_percentage (cluster-wide), per-tenant daily burst quota, anomaly detector (throttles allocator if burst pattern looks like traffic amplification attack), and automatic notification to tenant owners for bursts > 1 hour
Observability: dashboards for burst ingress rate, average burst duration, fairness index, preemption counts, and invoice estimates (real-time cost projection)
APIs: Add admin endpoints: POST /allocator/preview?tenant=X to simulate allocation and return cost estimate + preemption risk
Data retention: burst envelopes retained for 90 days for billing and 365 days for incident analysis.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable ephemeral-reservoir in staging for Canary tenants. Validate allocator decisions and billing exports (2-week soak).
Phase 2 (pilot): open to 10 committed Dedicated customers with opt-in and email notifications. Run for 4 weeks, collect invoice clarity feedback.
Phase 3 (gradual): enable in production with global max_burst_percentage=10% and per-tenant opt-out; monitor SLOs and billing disputes for 30 days.
Phase 4 (operator): ship Console controls and runbook; train support and SRE teams on revocation and dispute flow.

Rollback: global feature flag to disable ephemeral allocator and emit synthetic preemption to return ephemeral capacity quickly. If invoked, billing system will reconcile and mark in-flight envelopes as 'revoked' with special invoice notes.
testing_notes: Unit tests for allocator decision logic (priority weighting, decay math, preemption ordering)
Integration tests that simulate overlapping bursts across regions and assert committed SLO invariants remain satisfied
Billing integration e2e that verifies envelope consumption -> invoice line generation -> CSV export
Chaos test: simulate control-plane partition and ensure ephemeral allocations time out cleanly (no leaked billing records)
Load test scenarios: 30s spike, 5m sustained ramp, and repeated short bursts every minute to validate fairness decay prevents gaming
